snapshots.name: landing-1440
snapshots.text:
- main:
  - paragraph: a useful idea can start somewhere else. wildcard draws a niche specialist or an everyday concept, then asks an AI to bring back a concrete move for your problem.
  - paragraph: the cue changes the context. the question is what changes in the idea. a tool, an experiment, and a record of what held up.
  - paragraph: by christopher robin fiore · product design & AI research
  - heading "wildcard" [level=1]
  - region "inspectable cue draw":
    - paragraph: an outside starting point
    - text: mode=concept concept=tessellation lens=time-and-rhythm
    - paragraph: "now imagine thinking with this concept: tessellation. which relationship could be useful? this is a cue draw. generating ideas happens in your AI session. sha256-counter-v2 · dd81260fa657016337b0c564c55afb40728e009259bd78334e57e922eb91b4de"
    - button "draw another ↗"
    - button "copy command"
    - button "share draw"
    - button "auto draw"
    - status: draw ready. keep it, inspect it, or draw again.
    - group: inspect the receipt
  - complementary "figures":
    - heading "follow the evidence" [level=2]
    - text: the results, the revisions, the open question 01 · the question does naming an outside domain add useful new actions once its relation is already supplied? the new study separates the label from the relation.
    - link "inspect the counterfactual cue study ↗":
      - /url: case-study/#experiment
    - text: "02 · the new measured result the study did not resolve an advantage from naming the donor. named minus unnamed: -0.016 QNM@4, with a 95% interval from -0.109 to +0.063, across 32 briefs. amended measurement after one original judge block failed validation."
    - link "read the result and its limits ↗":
      - /url: case-study/#evidence
    - text: 03 · what the audit changed the first study had a negative quality result. later grading files contained missing or duplicated records. the legacy sampler coupled its choices. the original artifacts remain intact; corrections are published alongside them.
    - link "open the independent reanalysis ↗":
      - /url: https://github.com/globalanomalyindex/wildcard/tree/main/research/audit-2026-09
    - text: 04 · inspect the mechanism new draws carry a versioned seed and corpus receipt. old links replay the old sampler. sampling changes the prompt context; it does not modify model weights or certify an idea as true.
    - link "read the sampler specification ↗":
      - /url: https://github.com/globalanomalyindex/wildcard/blob/main/docs/sampler-v2.md
    - paragraph:
      - link "read the full case study →":
        - /url: case-study/
  - link "install, opens the case study":
    - /url: case-study/#install
    - text: install
  - paragraph:
    - text: 378 disciplines · 461 concepts · one inspectable draw
    - button "new draw"

    - text: 1 / 32 interaction accessibility
    - heading "Shared kiosk interruption" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Design a museum ticket kiosk flow for visitors who may need several minutes to read each screen. A session currently clears after 90 seconds, losing selected tickets. The next visitor must not see the previous visitor's selections. Staff can help but cannot monitor every kiosk.
    - group: constraints & success criteria
    - complementary:
      - paragraph: the relation held constant
      - paragraph: Records gain meaning from who created them and how they were grouped in the originating activity. Preserving those relationships supports interpretation even when a new arrangement would look tidier. Description can expose access paths without silently replacing the evidence of the original organization.
      - group: transfer boundary & source
    - group: inspect the independent reference bank · 12 actions
    - region "first condition":
      - text: first condition
      - combobox "first condition":
        - option "R · relation only" [selected]
        - option "LR · named relation"
        - option "S · strong direct prompt"
        - option "XR · mismatched name"
      - paragraph: the donor name is omitted from the prompt.
      - text: 0.0 QNM@4 · 3.0 qualified mechanisms · average of two judges
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - heading "Lock the session instead of deleting tickets" [level=3]
          - paragraph: Separate screen privacy from cart retention using a visitor-chosen local resume code, without an account.
          - group: implementation, check & evaluation
        - listitem:
          - heading "Provide an untimed, selection-free reading mode" [level=3]
          - paragraph: Let visitors read generic explanations indefinitely while their selected tickets remain locked and invisible.
          - group: implementation, check & evaluation
        - listitem:
          - heading "Discard personal details separately from ticket choices" [level=3]
          - paragraph: Minimize abandoned sensitive data without forcing visitors to rebuild their non-identifying ticket selections.
          - group: implementation, check & evaluation

        - option "S · strong direct prompt"
        - option "XR · mismatched name"
      - paragraph: "donor name: Archival provenance and original order"
      - text: 0.0 QNM@4 · 3.0 qualified mechanisms · average of two judges
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - heading "Replace destructive timeout with a protected pause." [level=3]
          - paragraph: Locally saved ticket selections survive masking; a visitor-created code unlocks them without an account.
          - group: implementation, check & evaluation
        - listitem:
          - heading "Collect personal details only at final checkout." [level=3]
          - paragraph: Separating ticket choices from sensitive checkout data limits what survives interruption without losing ticket-selection work.
          - group: implementation, check & evaluation
        - listitem:
          - heading "Make starting fresh an isolated, accessible handoff." [level=3]
          - paragraph: A new visitor gets a separate session, never a continuation of whichever draft was last active.
          - group: implementation, check & evaluation
      - link "open recorded response ↗":
        - /url: https://github.com/globalanomalyindex/wildcard/blob/main/research/transfer-v1/runs/main/calls/p01-LR/response.txt
    - paragraph:
      - text: these ratings come from the amended measurement panel. the original primary analysis halted after one judge supplied invalid reference IDs.
      - link "read the amendment":
        - /url: https://github.com/globalanomalyindex/wildcard/blob/main/research/transfer-v1/amendment.md
      - text: .
    - paragraph: QNM@4 counts distinct, qualified mechanisms absent from a separate baseline bank. scores average two model judges. novelty is relative to that bank; feasibility is judged, not demonstrated by implementation.

    - group: constraints & success criteria
    - complementary:
      - paragraph: the relation held constant
      - paragraph: A sequence can store only changes while unchanged values continue forward. Inserting one change can therefore affect later states until another explicit change overrides it. A local-only edit restores the former value at the next step, while a full state boundary can stop earlier changes propagating farther.

          - paragraph: Search the entire revision for exact text; use surrounding context to distinguish candidates, not similarity alone.
          - group: implementation, check & evaluation
        - listitem:

    - heading "hold the relation. change the name." [level=1]
    - paragraph: random cue injection has prior art. the narrower contribution is a donor-name intervention with explicit transfer boundaries and a baseline-relative mechanism measure.
    - article:
      - heading "what is controlled" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "every main condition gets the same brief and the same allowance: up to four actions, each no more than 110 words. R, LR, and XR receive the exact same relation and boundary. only the explicit domain name changes."

          - row "LR same relation + correct name":
            - rowheader "LR"
            - cell "same relation + correct name"
          - row "XR same relation + mismatched name":
            - rowheader "XR"
            - cell "same relation + mismatched name"
      - paragraph: this matches output allowance, not total tokens. actual usage and latency are recorded.
    - article:
      - heading "what gets counted" [level=2]
      - paragraph: a mechanism must respect the brief's constraints, be judged feasible, and describe an executable action with an observable check. duplicate mechanisms count once. when any candidate in a judge’s mechanism group matches the bank, every copy of that group is treated as non-new for that brief.
      - paragraph: "QNM@4 adds one more condition: the mechanism is absent from two separately generated baseline responses for that brief. the bank is never shown to the main generator."
      - paragraph: two masked judge configurations evaluate the actions. their scores are averaged within each brief. the brief is the analysis unit; judge votes do not increase the sample size.
      - link "full protocol, failures & statistical rules ↗":
        - /url: https://github.com/globalanomalyindex/wildcard/blob/main/research/transfer-v1/protocol.md
    - article:
      - heading "what this cannot establish" [level=2]
      - paragraph: these are authored synthetic briefs and model judgments. a relation can reveal its source even when unnamed. absence from a finite bank is not world originality. a feasible-looking proposal is not a shipped result.
      - paragraph: the requested generator is gpt-6-astra; judges request gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.5. provider-returned snapshots are not exposed by the Codex CLI transport and are recorded as unknown.
      - paragraph: separate counterfactual fixtures check relation following and boundary handling. they are not proof of creativity or the cause of any main-study effect.
      - link "prior art & contribution boundaries ↗":
        - /url: https://github.com/globalanomalyindex/wildcard/blob/main/research/transfer-v1/related-work.md
    - article:
      - heading "a measurement failure, kept in the record." [level=2]
      - paragraph: one of the original 64 judge blocks used candidate IDs where bank references were required. the frozen protocol halted the primary analysis. all 64 blocks were then remeasured under a published amendment, with reference IDs constrained to the correct bank. generated ideas, prompts and scoring stayed fixed; the two panels were not pooled.
      - paragraph: the result reported here is an amended measurement on the same generated sample, not a completed original primary test or an independent replication.

- main:
  - region "hold the relation. change the name.":
    - paragraph: a testable question, not a neural metaphor
    - heading "hold the relation. change the name." [level=1]
    - paragraph: random cue injection has prior art. the narrower contribution is a donor-name intervention with explicit transfer boundaries and a baseline-relative mechanism measure.
    - article:
      - heading "what is controlled" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "every main condition gets the same brief and the same allowance: up to four actions, each no more than 110 words. R, LR, and XR receive the exact same relation and boundary. only the explicit domain name changes."
      - table "the four prompt conditions":
        - caption: the four prompt conditions
        - rowgroup:
          - row "condition outside information":
            - columnheader "condition"
            - columnheader "outside information"
        - rowgroup:
          - row "S strong direct prompt, no cue":
            - rowheader "S"
            - cell "strong direct prompt, no cue"
          - row "R relation + boundary":
            - rowheader "R"
            - cell "relation + boundary"
          - row "LR same relation + correct name":
            - rowheader "LR"
            - cell "same relation + correct name"
          - row "XR same relation + mismatched name":
            - rowheader "XR"
            - cell "same relation + mismatched name"
      - paragraph: this matches output allowance, not total tokens. actual usage and latency are recorded.
    - article:
      - heading "what gets counted" [level=2]
      - paragraph: a mechanism must respect the brief's constraints, be judged feasible, and describe an executable action with an observable check. duplicate mechanisms count once. when any candidate in a judge’s mechanism group matches the bank, every copy of that group is treated as non-new for that brief.
      - paragraph: "QNM@4 adds one more condition: the mechanism is absent from two separately generated baseline responses for that brief. the bank is never shown to the main generator."
      - paragraph: two masked judge configurations evaluate the actions. their scores are averaged within each brief. the brief is the analysis unit; judge votes do not increase the sample size.
      - link "full protocol, failures & statistical rules ↗":
        - /url: https://github.com/globalanomalyindex/wildcard/blob/main/research/transfer-v1/protocol.md
    - article:
      - heading "what this cannot establish" [level=2]
      - paragraph: these are authored synthetic briefs and model judgments. a relation can reveal its source even when unnamed. absence from a finite bank is not world originality. a feasible-looking proposal is not a shipped result.
      - paragraph: the requested generator is gpt-6-astra; judges request gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.5. provider-returned snapshots are not exposed by the Codex CLI transport and are recorded as unknown.
      - paragraph: separate counterfactual fixtures check relation following and boundary handling. they are not proof of creativity or the cause of any main-study effect.
      - link "prior art & contribution boundaries ↗":
        - /url: https://github.com/globalanomalyindex/wildcard/blob/main/research/transfer-v1/related-work.md
    - article:
      - heading "a measurement failure, kept in the record." [level=2]
      - paragraph: one of the original 64 judge blocks used candidate IDs where bank references were required. the frozen protocol halted the primary analysis. all 64 blocks were then remeasured under a published amendment, with reference IDs constrained to the correct bank. generated ideas, prompts and scoring stayed fixed; the two panels were not pooled.
      - paragraph: the result reported here is an amended measurement on the same generated sample, not a completed original primary test or an independent replication.
      - link "failure, amendment & frozen rules ↗":
        - /url: https://github.com/globalanomalyindex/wildcard/blob/main/research/transfer-v1/amendment.md
    - group: separate counterfactual checks · 6/8 pairs passed the exact contract
